lines: I feel like I'm staying forever inside the fog.
I stroke the scar, exhale, then bite my lips again to get through it.
A consolation that feels like a collection of worn‑out words.
A hypocrite who spits it out with a knowing look.
"Don't stop," "I won't forgive,"
"It's irresponsible," "That's impossible,"
The me who lived in the past says,
"Laugh," "Laugh," I say.
The rain that suddenly starts falling
doesn't conveniently stop.
We, who have lost our umbrellas,
are just shouting hoarsely in the dark.
I searched for you on a night I couldn't cry.
I thought we'd keep living together just like this.
Don't leave me alone.
Don't.
Don't.
Don't.
I feel like I'm staying forever at the bottom of the sea.
I barely emit heat,
then pretend I'm alive again, like a fool.
It's fine to be praised, since I'm laughing like this.
I'm not causing any trouble, right?
"What on earth is whose fault?"
"How did it come to this?"
"I can't forgive,"
The overly childish me cried.
Please, save that version of me, okay?
The rain that suddenly starts falling
doesn't conveniently stop.
We, who have lost our umbrellas,
are just shouting hoarsely in the dark.
It feels like I'm forever at the bottom of a dream.
I couldn't stop the hand that stroked the scar, so I say,
"I killed the me of that day; it's unfair now."
The rain that suddenly starts falling
doesn't conveniently stop.
We, who have lost our umbrellas,
let our hoarse voices drift through the crowd.
I searched for you to a pathetic degree.
I thought we'd keep living together just like this.
Don't leave me alone.
Don't.
Don't.
